paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this whole chapter: Solomon is handing you a toolbox for living with other people. Speak the right word at the right time, because "A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver" (Proverbs 25:11). Keep your promises, because "clouds and wind without rain" is the man who boasts of gifts never given (Proverbs 25:14). And a man who bears false witness against his neighbor is like a club or a sword or a sharp arrow (Proverbs 25:18).

Now here's the part that surprised me: a lot of these pictures are about holding back. Eat just the honey you need (Proverbs 25:16), and be patient, because "a gentle tongue can break a bone" (Proverbs 25:15). The last picture says it all: "Like a city whose walls are broken down is a man who does not control his temper" (Proverbs 25:28). I once told myself ONE more spoonful of dough, and friend, I have never been the same.

So what do you do with it? Start small, with the next word you say and the next time you want to win. Even toward an enemy, Solomon says give food to the hungry one and water to the thirsty one, and "the LORD will reward you" (Proverbs 25:21-22). You don't have to be perfect at this. You just keep picking up one wise word at a time, the way Hezekiah's men kept copying them down (Proverbs 25:1).
